-- Routes table for V2.5 integration
CREATE TABLE routes (
    route_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    distance_miles DECIMAL(8,2),
    elevation_gain INT,
    difficulty ENUM('easy','moderate','difficult','expert'),
    route_type ENUM('loop','out-and-back','point-to-point','figure-8'),
    gpx_data LONGTEXT,
    created_by CHAR(36),
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    is_public BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE
);

-- Waypoints table for trailhead management
CREATE TABLE waypoints (
    waypoint_id CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    latitude DECIMAL(10,7) NOT NULL,
    longitude DECIMAL(10,7) NOT NULL,
    type ENUM('trailhead','staging','hazard','poi') DEFAULT 'poi',
    description TEXT,
    created_by CHAR(36),
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    deleted_at DATETIME NULL
);

=== GroupTrack_V3_Online_Offline_Manual_v2.docx ===
GroupTrack
V3.0 Online / Offline Manual
Features, Functions, and Intent
v2  |  April 18, 2026  |  CONFIDENTIAL
Revisions from v1
First-time setup is three steps — Sign In, accept combined Terms & Policy, Dashboard — not four
Terms & Policy is a single existing document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy
Subscription mechanics simplified: hardcoded subscribed for all signed-in users during initial V3.0
'Coming Soon' is reserved for mapping functions that are moving to V2.5 — all other incomplete features show placeholders describing intent
iPad implementation noted as pending Monday planning decision — V2.5 or V3.0
1. What GroupTrack Is
GroupTrack is an off-grid awareness platform for any group activity in areas without cell service. It is designed for off-road vehicles, hikers, mountain bikers, overlanders, search and rescue teams, and hunting parties — anyone who needs to coordinate with others in places where phones stop working.

The platform combines three capabilities into a single Android app:
Real-time group position awareness over LoRa mesh radio — no cell tower required
Organized ride management — create, invite, enroll, broadcast — all before you lose signal
Offline maps and trail overlays — downloaded in advance, available everywhere

1.1 The Core Idea — Online Before, Offline During
GroupTrack splits its functionality along one essential boundary: what happens online before a ride, and what happens offline during a ride.
Before the ride, while you still have connectivity, the cloud handles coordination work — creating rides, sending invites, downloading maps, applying radio configurations. Everything gets prepared, downloaded, and cached to the device.
During the ride, when you are out of cell range, everything runs locally. The mesh radio handles position updates between riders. The map tiles are already on the device. The ride configuration is already on the radio. No network calls happen while you are actually riding.

Key principle: the radio never needs the cloud. Authentication failures, network outages, or server problems never interrupt an active ride. Once you have prepared online, the ride works offline — always.
1.2 Platform Support
V3.0 ships for Android. iPad support is under active planning for a future release (V2.5 or V3.0 — to be confirmed). Web-based access and a native iOS port are on the roadmap for later releases.
2. Understanding Feature States in V3.0
As you explore V3.0 you will encounter screens in one of three states. Understanding these helps set expectations for what each screen can do right now.


Why the split? V2.5 is delivering a standalone trail product that addresses mapping functionality in depth — including map source stability, Utah OHV overlays, and a new Planning Map architecture. V3.0 focuses on cloud-based ride coordination. Each release has a clear purpose, and users get a stable foundation at each step.
3. Online vs. Offline Services
GroupTrack presents two service categories. Which one you interact with depends on whether you have connectivity and what you are trying to accomplish.


3.1 How the App Decides Which Mode You Are In
Every app launch, GroupTrack checks three things:
Do I have cached sign-in credentials? (Am I a returning user?)
Is there network connectivity right now?
Are my accepted Terms & Policy version current?
Based on the answers, the app routes you to the right starting screen — the Dashboard if everything is current and you are online, the Convoy Map if you are offline, or sign-in if you are new.
4. Getting Started
4.1 First Install
When you install GroupTrack for the first time, the app launches into a sign-in flow. You need to be connected to Wi-Fi or cell data the first time — account creation requires network access. After first-time setup, the app works offline.

First-time setup is three steps:
Sign In with Google — tap the Google sign-in button, choose your account
Accept the Terms & Policy — a single combined document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy
Dashboard — you have landed on the main online services screen

Not ready to sign in? The Skip for now link on the sign-in screen takes you directly to the Convoy Map. You can use offline features (tile download, radio config, import GPX/KML) without an account. Sign in any time later from the menu.

4.2 Terms & Policy
GroupTrack uses a single combined Terms & Policy document that covers:
Rider Terms — how riders use the app and participate in rides
Organizer Terms — additional terms that apply when you become an organizer and create rides
Privacy Policy — what information is collected and how it is shared (notably: your name and email are shared with organizers of rides you follow or enroll in)
The document is shown in full during sign-up. If the document is updated, you are prompted to re-accept the new version on your next app launch.
4.3 What Sign-In Unlocks
Signing in enables all online features. After your first successful sign-in, you can use online features any time you have network access. Offline features are always available whether you sign in or not.


4.4 Subscription Status
GroupTrack operates on a freemium model. Most features are free forever. Organizer features and online ride management are part of the $3.00/month subscription tier.

For the initial V3.0 release, all signed-in users receive full subscription access at no cost. A go-live date will be announced when subscription billing activates. Users active during this period will be notified in advance and will retain access to their ride history and downloaded data regardless of subscription status.
5. Online Features
Online features require network connectivity and a signed-in account. They are organized around the Dashboard, which is the landing screen after sign-in.
5.1 Dashboard
Dashboard is the landing screen for all online services. It is a live data screen, not a button launcher. Three sections stack vertically from top to bottom:
Notifications — system announcements, ride updates, broadcast messages from organizers you follow
Enrollments — rides you are enrolled in, upcoming first, then active, then recently completed
Invites — pending invitations awaiting your accept or decline
Each entry is tappable for more detail. Invites have inline ACCEPT and DECLINE buttons. Enrollments have a VIEW DETAILS button that takes you to the full ride record.
The bottom navigation bar on the Dashboard provides access to the other main online sections: Rides, Explore, Tracks, Profile, Field Radio.
5.2 My Rides
The My Rides screen organizes your rides into tabs:
ALL — every ride you have any relationship to
ENROLLED — rides you have enrolled in as a rider
ORGANIZED — rides you have created as an organizer
COMPLETED — rides that have ended
Tap any ride to see its detail screen — trailhead, planned route, enrollment list, organizer contact. Organizers can also send invites and broadcast messages from this screen.
5.3 Create Ride (Organizer)
Any signed-in user can become an organizer and create rides. The organizer upgrade is available from the Profile screen and is covered by the same combined Terms & Policy document — no separate acceptance flow is needed beyond confirming the upgrade.

Creating a ride requires:
Ride name
Date
Trailhead — selected by tapping the map or picking from your waypoint library
Map area — bounding box for tile download, drawn on the map or defined by an existing route
Description (optional)
Public or private visibility
The SAVE RIDE button stays disabled until both trailhead and map area are set. These gates are highlighted in orange so you know what is missing.
When the ride is saved, GroupTrack automatically generates a unique radio channel name (CONVOY-XXXX) and a random channel PSK. These travel with the ride to every rider who enrolls, so everyone ends up with matching radio configuration.
5.4 Send Invite and Broadcast
From a ride's detail screen, organizers have two ways to invite riders.
Send Invite — Targeted
Send Invite generates a single-use invite link. Share it via:
QR code — display on screen, another person scans with their phone
Copy Link — copies the invite URL to the clipboard
Share Sheet — uses the Android system share sheet for text, email, or messaging apps
Invite link format: grouptrack.org/invite/{token}
Broadcast — Followers
Broadcast sends the ride notification to everyone who follows you as an organizer. Broadcasts are one-time per ride — once sent, the ride is broadcast and cannot be rebroadcast to the same follower list.
5.5 Accept Invite
Tapping an invite link (or scanning the QR code) opens the Invite Accept screen. You see the ride name, date, organizer, a download warning, and a summary of what accepting means.
Accepting does four things:
Downloads the ride JSON to local storage
Starts automatic map tile download for the ride's map area
Sets a flag marking the radio ready to accept the ride's channel configuration
Creates an enrollment record tying you to the ride
You are also offered the option to add the ride to your calendar.
5.6 Explore Rides
Explore shows public rides that organizers have chosen to list publicly. Search by zip + radius, map area, or organizer name. Each public ride shows a small map vignette with the staging area marked, the date, the organizer's contact info, and a FOLLOW option.
5.7 Profile
The Profile screen shows your account information and related entries:
Your name, email, and subscription status
Callsign, vehicle type, zip code (editable)
Email opt-in toggle for broadcasts
Become Organizer upgrade
Ride History link
Following link
Sign Out button
5.8 Ride History
Ride History shows every ride you have participated in, most recent first. For each ride you see:
Name, date, organizer
Organizer's email
Full rider list with email addresses
EXPORT GPX button to save the ride's track to Downloads
Entries can be searched by name, date, or riding area.
5.9 Following
Following is your list of organizers whose rides and broadcasts you want to see. For each organizer you can see their name, email, and optionally phone. Unfollow any time.
5.10 Track Library
Track Library is a public repository of ride tracks donated by participants of organized rides. Filter and search by difficulty, riding area, or recommendation percentage. Tap any track for its detail — map preview, difficulty, recommend %, donor name, and a DOWNLOAD TO DEVICE button. Downloading a track also auto-downloads the map tiles for its area.
6. Offline Features
Offline features work anywhere, with or without network connectivity, and regardless of sign-in status. These are the core operational capabilities — what the app does during a ride.
6.1 Convoy Map
The Convoy Map is the main operational screen. It runs as a background process whenever the app is open. The Convoy Map shows three behaviors based on what is happening, called RideStates:


Lead Lock
In CONVOY and ORGANIZED states, the Convoy Map automatically tracks the lead cart. A Lead Lock slider in settings configures the distance threshold (300 to 1500 feet, default 330 feet) at which a rider is considered the leader.
RECORD and STOP
RECORD starts GPS track recording. STOP ends the recording and prompts for a track name. In ORGANIZED state, STOP also offers a survey (difficulty, recommendation, track donation) before saving.
Map Settings
The Map Settings panel offers: Offline/Online tile toggle, Map type selector (Satellite, Hybrid, Topo), Track Lead Only, Show Downloaded Areas, Track format (GPX/KML), Tile Download Region entry, Zoom range (Z14 to Z18), Overlay Selector entry.
6.2 Map Manager — Coming Soon in V2.5
Map Manager is the comprehensive planning map toolset — tile download regions, waypoint creation, route planning, overlay management, Utah OHV trail data. In V3.0, the Map Manager entry point shows a Coming Soon notice because this functionality is being delivered in V2.5 via a dedicated Planning Map architecture.

Why is Map Manager delivered in V2.5 instead of V3.0? V2.5 is a standalone trail product release focused on map foundation work — multiple map sources, Utah OHV GeoJSON overlays, a new Planning Map separate from the operational Convoy Map. This structure avoids touching Convoy Map's hard-won stability while building out planning features in depth.

Map functions arriving in V2.5's Planning Map:
Find Area — viewport, geocoder, name search, waypoint radius search
Tile Download — draw a region, pick zoom levels, download tiles
Import GPX/KML — bring in tracks and routes from files
Overlay Selector — pick routes, tracks, waypoints to display
Waypoint Library — manage trailheads, staging areas, hazards, POIs
Route Planner — draw routes by tapping waypoints
Utah OHV overlay — motorized vehicle trail data (ships in V2.4 and V2.5)

V3.0 integration points for organized rides (Set Trailhead picker, Set Map Area picker) reference the V2.5 Planning Map once available.
6.3 Field Radio
The Field Radio screen is the interface to the connected LoRa mesh radio. Always accessible, online or offline, signed in or not. The screen shows:
BLE connection status
Active channel name and frequency
Spreading factor and transmit power
Current callsign
Main actions:
Apply Ride Config — push the current ride's channel and PSK to the radio
Apply Master Config — push the master GroupTrack radio configuration
Verify Config — read back the radio's settings and compare to expected
Change Long Name to LEAD — set callsign to LEAD for the lead rider
Bluetooth Toggle Reconnect — cycle BLE to recover from disconnects

Applying ride config is what gates participation in an organized ride. If your radio does not have the correct channel and PSK, you are invisible to the organized mesh. Apply ride config before leaving the trailhead.
6.4 Archive and Restore
The Archive and Restore screen manages saved radio configurations. Every time you apply a new configuration, the previous one is automatically archived. You can restore any archive to quickly revert. Archives are listed by date and time with a human-readable summary.
6.5 Import GPX/KML
Import GPX/KML lets you bring tracks and routes from outside sources. Flow:
Tap Import GPX/KML
Android file picker opens
Choose Route or Track
Give it a name
MD5 duplicate check runs
File saved to local library; appears in Overlay Selector
6.6 Your Tracks

iPad implementation scope (V2.5 vs V3.0) flagged for Monday's planning discussion — not resolved in this document
1. Purpose and Scope
This document specifies the complete V3.0 registration flow and the stubbed paywall design. It is the gate document for V3.0 walkaway: until registration is built, stubbed-function definitions cannot be meaningfully reviewed because most V3 stubs depend on an authenticated user_id.

Registration is the entry point for all V3.0 online functionality. Every downstream screen (Dashboard, My Rides, Create Ride, Invite, Explore, Profile, Track Library) depends on a valid user_id cached locally from the registration flow.

Scope:
Registration flow — s01 Sign In through s04 Dashboard, including the combined Terms & Policy screen
Session persistence — SharedPreferences cache fields, offline behavior, re-acceptance triggers
Paywall as stub — s01b built and navigable; isSubscribed hardcoded true at walkaway
Online/Offline auth boundary
Go-Live activation steps — the minimum set of code changes to flip subscription from stub to live
Build inventory — what exists, what needs completion, per file
2. Stub and Placeholder UX Pattern
V3.0 walkaway produces a fully navigable app. Every screen in the V3 user flow opens and does something sensible. Three states exist for any given screen:


No non-mapping screen in V3.0 shows a 'Coming Soon' banner. Either the screen works, or it clearly describes its intent as a placeholder. This ensures V3.0 is a complete-feeling product at walkaway even though Phase C wiring continues toward go-live.
3. Registration Flow Overview
Registration runs top-to-bottom exactly once per user on the installed device. After successful completion, subsequent app launches use cached credentials and route directly to the Dashboard (s04) or the Convoy Map depending on online state.

3.1 Top-Level Launch Routing
App launch
   |
   v
ConvoySessionManager.resolveLaunchRoute(context)
   |
   |-- No cached user_id          --> s01 Sign In
   |-- Cached, terms current      --> s04 Dashboard
   |-- Cached, terms outdated     --> s02 Terms & Policy (re-accept)
   |-- Cached, offline            --> Convoy Map (never blocks radio)

4.1  s01 — Sign In
File: ConvoySignInScreen.kt (EXISTS, partial)
Purpose
First-time authentication entry point. Google One Tap acquires a Google ID token, exchanged for a GroupTrack user_id via POST /users/register.

User selects account, grants profile scope
SDK returns ID token, email, first/last name
App calls ConvoyApiClient.registerUser()
On success, user_id cached via ConvoySessionManager.saveUser()
Route directly to s02 Terms & Policy (paywall bypassed by hardcoded isSubscribed=true)
Error Handling
Google Sign-In failure: error banner, offer retry or Skip for now
Network failure during registration: cache Google creds, mark registration_pending=true, route to Convoy Map, retry on connectivity

Display and capture acceptance of the single combined Terms and Policy document covering rider terms, organizer terms, and privacy policy. Version tracking triggers re-acceptance when the document is updated.

Rider Terms, Organizer Terms, and Privacy Policy are a single document that already exists. There is no separate Privacy screen, no separate Organizer Terms screen at signup. s06 Become Organizer references this same document for organizer-specific acceptance at upgrade time.

UI Elements
Document title and version (e.g., 'GroupTrack Terms & Policy v1.0')
Scrollable document body (loaded from asset file or GET /terms)
Section anchors for quick navigation: Rider Terms, Organizer Terms, Privacy
I ACCEPT checkbox
CONTINUE button (disabled until checkbox checked)
Decline and Exit link
Behavior
Load current terms version from GET /terms (fall back to bundled asset if offline)
Display document with version header
User reviews, checks I ACCEPT, taps CONTINUE
Cache accepted version: SharedPreferences key terms_accepted = version string
POST /users/accept-terms with user_id, version, timestamp
Route to s04 Dashboard
Version Mismatch Re-Acceptance
On every launch, compare cached terms_accepted against the current published version. Mismatch triggers routing to s02 on next sign-in regardless of other state. Cached version updated only on fresh acceptance.

5.2 Hardcoded isSubscribed — Walkaway Implementation
The isSubscribed() function is the single point of control for subscription gating. At walkaway it is hardcoded to return true. Activation instructions are embedded as comments inside the function so there is no external config to find, no flag to remember, no ambiguity.

// ConvoySessionManager.kt

/**
 * Returns true if the user has an active subscription.
 *
 * WALKAWAY STATE: Hardcoded to return true for all signed-in users.
 * This allows full V3.0 feature access without subscription billing.
 *
 * TO ACTIVATE SUBSCRIPTION BILLING AT GO-LIVE:
 *   1. Comment out the hardcoded 'return true' below
 *   2. Uncomment the expires_at check block
 *   3. Ensure users.expires_at is being updated by the receipt
 *      verification endpoint (convoy_api.php POST /billing/verify)
 *   4. Ensure Google Play Billing SDK is wired (see ConvoyBillingClient.kt)
 *   5. Update /users/register to stop setting expires_at = 2099-12-31
 *
 * No other code changes are required anywhere else in the app.
 * Every subscription gate calls isSubscribed() — change this, change all.
 */
fun isSubscribed(ctx: Context): Boolean {
    // WALKAWAY: return true for all signed-in users
    if (!isSignedIn(ctx)) return false
    return true

    // GO-LIVE: uncomment the block below, remove 'return true' above
    //
    // val expires = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, 0)
    //     .getLong(KEY_EXPIRES_AT, 0L)
    // return expires > System.currentTimeMillis()
}

5.3 Key API Surface on ConvoySessionManager
fun isSignedIn(ctx: Context): Boolean
fun isSubscribed(ctx: Context): Boolean  // Hardcoded true at walkaway (see 5.2)
fun saveUser(ctx, userId, googleId, email, firstName, lastName)
fun getUserId(ctx: Context): String?
fun clearSession(ctx: Context)  // Sign out
fun resolveLaunchRoute(ctx, onlineAvailable: Boolean): LaunchRoute
fun acceptTerms(ctx: Context, version: String)
fun needsTermsReaccept(ctx: Context, currentVersion: String): Boolean

5.4 LaunchRoute Enum
enum class LaunchRoute {
    SIGN_IN,        // No cached user_id
    SUBSCRIPTION,   // Post go-live only; never reached at walkaway
    TERMS,          // Cached user_id, terms version mismatch
    DASHBOARD,      // All checks pass
    CONVOY_MAP      // Offline or Skip-for-now
}
6. API Endpoints — Registration Flow
File: ConvoyApiClient.kt (EXISTS)
Base URL: https://34.224.89.217/  (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)


6.1 Request/Response Contracts
POST /users/register
Request:  { google_id, email, first_name, last_name }
Response: { user_id: UUID, expires_at: datetime, is_new: bool }
At walkaway: PHP sets expires_at = 2099-12-31 for all registrations. At go-live: expires_at is set by receipt verification flow.
7. Online / Offline Behavior
KEY PRINCIPLE: Authentication state must never block radio operation. Mesh map, HUD, GPS tracking, radio config always work using locally cached data.


7.1 Pending Registration Recovery
If Google succeeds but POST /users/register fails, user is NOT forced back through Google sign-in on next attempt:
Google creds (id, email, names) cached with registration_pending=true
User routed to Convoy Map with banner: 'Sign-in pending — online features available once connected'
On every launch and connectivity change, background task retries using cached Google creds
On success, user_id cached, registration_pending cleared, s02 Terms flow triggered on next app resume
8. Paywall Stub Design Summary
8.1 Stub Mechanism
s01b paywall screen is FULLY BUILT and navigable from dev menu
isSubscribed() hardcoded to return true (see section 5.2)
resolveLaunchRoute() never routes to SUBSCRIPTION at walkaway because isSubscribed is always true
All subscription-gated screens (Dashboard, Rides, Invite, Explore, etc.) behave as if user is subscribed
users.expires_at in RDS set to 2099-12-31 for walkaway-era registrations (backup belt-and-suspenders)
Dashboard profile shows 'SUBSCRIBED' status badge

8.2 What Makes This a Safe Stub
Single point of control — only isSubscribed() changes at go-live. No scattered flags to find.
Self-documenting — activation instructions live inside the function body, not in a separate config doc.
Screen stays testable — dev menu force-route keeps s01b exercised through walkaway testing.
Reversible — hardcoded true can be re-enabled instantly if go-live encounters issues.

1. Document Purpose & Scope
This inventory catalogs all 29 atomic stubbed processes in GroupTrack V3.0, derived from comprehensive where_used analysis, real database schema inspection, and existing PHP API evaluation. Each process has explicit implementation requirements to eliminate rediscovery in future development cycles.
1.1 Process Identification Methodology
where_used analysis: traced function calls to identify stub patterns and integration points
Database schema inspection: documented all 66+ fields across 5 tables
PHP API gap analysis: identified 80% of database capabilities unused by current API
Android integration mapping: connected UI screens to backend requirements
1.2 Key Findings
Database capability mismatch: Sophisticated 66-field schema vs basic 20-field API usage
Advanced features already in database: map bounds, location services, terms tracking, status workflows
Implementation strategy: expand existing PHP patterns rather than rebuild from scratch
Implementation Reality: Database supports advanced features that current PHP API doesn't expose. V3.0 completion = API expansion, not database redesign.
2. Core API Backend Processes
Primary backend integration processes derived from ConvoyApiClient method signatures and real database schema requirements.
3. Dashboard Data Feed Processes
Real-time data endpoints for ConvoyDashboardScreen.kt. UI components expect these feeds but currently display placeholder data.
4. V2.5 Map Integration Processes
Advanced mapping processes for V2.5 Planning Map integration. Database already supports map_bounds, trailhead_waypoint_id, route_id fields.
5. User Management & Session Processes
User account and session management. Database has 23 user fields but PHP API only uses 6 basic fields.
6. Content & Community Processes
Community content sharing and discovery features. Requires new database tables for track library and rating system.
7. GPS & Location Services
Location tracking and GPS services integration. Connects V2.4 convoy tracking with V3.0 community features.
8. Communication & Notification Systems
User communication, notifications, and messaging infrastructure for platform engagement.
9. Implementation Strategy & Priorities
Ordered implementation sequence based on user impact, technical dependencies, and platform value delivery.
9.1 Critical Path (V3.0 Launch Blockers)
SP01-SP06: Core API backend processes - expand existing PHP to use full database schema
SP07-SP09: Dashboard data feeds - implement missing GET endpoints for live data
SP17: Subscription validation - implement expires_at timestamp checking
9.2 High Value (Major Feature Enablers)
SP10-SP14: V2.5 Map Manager integration - connect advanced mapping to V3.0 services
SP15-SP16: User profile completion - use all 23 database fields for rich profiles
SP26-SP28: Communication systems - notifications, email, real-time updates
9.3 Community Features (Network Effects)
SP19-SP22: Content sharing system - track library and community ratings
SP23-SP25: Location services - proximity discovery and local recommendations
SP29: In-app messaging - enhanced coordination tools
9.4 Technical Dependencies
Database expansion: SP19-SP22 require new tables (ride_tracks, track_ratings)
V2.5 integration: SP10-SP14 depend on Map Manager completion
Infrastructure services: SP26-SP28 require external service integration (Firebase, AWS SES)
10. Success Metrics & Validation
Measurable criteria for determining successful implementation and platform readiness.
10.1 Implementation Completion
All 29 processes have status WORKING (no PLACEHOLDER or MISSING)
PHP API uses >80% of available database fields (currently ~20%)
End-to-end user workflows completable without mock data
V2.5 Map Manager fully integrated with V3.0 services
10.2 Platform Capability
Location-based organizer discovery functional
Community content sharing operational
Real-time notifications and updates working
Premium feature gates functional but disabled
10.3 Deployment Readiness
Value-first service delivery complete (all features free)
Billing infrastructure ready but disabled
Database performance optimized with proper indexing
Monitoring and error tracking operational
Implementation Success = 29 WORKING processes + full database utilization + V2.5 integration + value-first service delivery

curl -s http://localhost/ | head -5
Should return the first 5 lines of the HTML. Then test in browser: http://34.224.89.217

Lifecycle Phase Legend
RULE: Any function tagged INIT must NOT require permissions, network, or launch activities. Any function tagged TICK must have permission guard if it accesses GPS/Location.

1. Meshtastic Base Layer Modifications
These are changes made to files OUTSIDE the convoy/ package. Stock Meshtastic does not have these. Every change here runs during app startup and affects ALL users.
1.1 MainActivity.kt
1.2 ui/Main.kt
1.3 navigation/ConvoyNavigation.kt
1.4 app/build.gradle.kts
1.5 AndroidManifest.xml

2. ConvoyViewModel.kt — Critical Path Analysis
47 functions. This is the heart of the convoy system. Every tick cycle, every GPS call, every state update flows through here.
2.1 INIT Phase — Runs During App Startup
WARNING: Everything in init{} runs on the MAIN THREAD during Activity.onCreate(). No permissions are granted yet. No UI is visible. Any blocking call here causes ANR.
ISSUE: scanImportDirectory() runs in init via viewModelScope.launch. It queries MediaStore which may require storage permission. On a fresh install this may fail silently or block.
2.2 TICK Phase — Runs Every 3–5 Seconds
WARNING: tick() runs from init{} before map loads. Permission guard added in efa1b677e.

=== GroupTrack_day23_plan (1).docx ===
GroupTrack.org
Day 23 Plan
March 23, 2026  |  Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride  |  kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android

Priority 1 — Radio Write Persistence
WorkingConfig is wiped every time the user navigates to the Meshtastic connections screen. Two separate radio reset functions are the cause. This is a field-blocking issue — the organizer cannot pair a radio mid-session without losing all config work. Must be fixed before field deployment.

Priority 2 — GPS Broadcast Interval Slider
Smart position broadcast interval is fixed in master config. Riders in fast-moving convoys need more frequent updates; slower rides can conserve battery with longer intervals. Slider reads live from radio, writes back only if changed — no reboot required for position config changes.

=== GroupTrack_day23_plan.docx ===
GroupTrack.org
Day 23 Plan
March 23, 2026  |  Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride  |  kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android

Priority 1 — Radio Write Persistence
WorkingConfig is wiped every time the user navigates to the Meshtastic connections screen. Two separate radio reset functions are the cause. This is a field-blocking issue — the organizer cannot pair a radio mid-session without losing all config work. Must be fixed before field deployment.

Priority 2 — GPS Broadcast Interval Slider
Smart position broadcast interval is fixed in master config. Riders in fast-moving convoys need more frequent updates; slower rides can conserve battery with longer intervals. Slider reads live from radio, writes back only if changed — no reboot required for position config changes.

GroupTrack.org
Product Roadmap v7
Last Updated: March 22, 2026  |  Author: Fred Kix  |  Repo: kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android
Platform Overview
GroupTrack.org is a Meshtastic-based off-grid group ride coordination system built as a fork of the Meshtastic Android client. It provides real-time mesh networking for vehicle convoys, event ride organization, and field coordination without cellular dependency. Domain: GroupTrack.org.


Product Tiers and Pricing

V1 — Manual Setup Group Ride Tracker


V2 — Self-Service Setup + Backend Ride Registration

V2 Architecture

V2 Radio Config Engine — COMPLETE March 19, 2026


V2 Backend Ride Registration — IN PROGRESS March 22, 2026


V2 Pending Features

Backend Architecture — V2
Database Schema — AWS RDS MySQL

Ride Registration Flow

Riders pull ride configuration to automatically customize their radio settings and download map tiles for the ride area. Includes full ride definition, invite distribution, and map pre-loading. Designed for recurring group rides with unique channel and configuration requirements.

enrollments | ride_id | UUID FK | References rides.ride_id

enrollments | enrolled_at | DATETIME | Enrollment timestamp
invites | invite_id | UUID PK | Unique invite identifier
invites | ride_id | UUID FK | References rides.ride_id
invites | invited_by | UUID FK | References users.user_id — organizer only
invites | invite_token | VARCHAR | Unique random token — this IS the invite link
invites | claimed_by | UUID FK | Null until claimed by rider
invites | created_at | DATETIME | Invite creation timestamp
invites | claimed_at | DATETIME | Null until claimed

1 | Organizer | Creates ride in app (online) — stored in MySQL
2 | Organizer | Sends invite link via any method (SMS, email, WhatsApp)
3 | Rider | Taps invite link — GroupTrack.org opens via deep link
4 | App | Calls GET /ride/{invite_token} — downloads ride JSON
5 | App | Saves ride JSON to local DB — marks invite claimed
6 | Rider | Goes offline — applies ride config to radio via existing engine

=== GroupTrack_QuickStart_Installation_Troubleshooting_v1.md ===
# GroupTrack â€” Quick Start, Installation & Troubleshooting
## Tester and Developer Reference
## Updated May 9, 2026

---

## QUICK START

### Before Your First Ride

1. Install GroupTrack APK on your Android device (see Installation below)
2. Power on your T1000-E Meshtastic radio
3. Open GroupTrack â€” radio should connect via Bluetooth automatically
4. Verify connection: radio icon shows connected in the app

### âš ï¸ CRITICAL â€” Two Radio Restrictions

**RESTRICTION 1 â€” T1000-E Firmware: DO NOT update beyond 2.6.11**

The T1000-E Meshtastic radio firmware MUST stay at version 2.6.11 or earlier. Updating to any firmware version beyond 2.6.11 will make the radio unstable for Bluetooth connectivity and radio configuration. This is a known issue with newer Meshtastic firmware on the T1000-E hardware.

- Check current firmware: Meshtastic app â†’ Radio Config â†’ Device Info
- If firmware is 2.6.11 or earlier: DO NOT UPDATE
- If firmware was accidentally updated beyond 2.6.11: flash back to 2.6.11 using Meshtastic Flasher tool
- This restriction applies to ALL T1000-E radios used with GroupTrack

**RESTRICTION 2 â€” Keep Radio Within Bluetooth Range During Rides**

When riding, ALWAYS keep your radio in your cart/vehicle within 50 feet of your phone. Do NOT carry the radio away from your phone (or vice versa) beyond Bluetooth effective range.

- Bluetooth effective range: approximately 50 feet (15 meters)
- If radio exceeds BLE range while still "connected," the connection enters supervision timeout
- Symptoms: app freezes/pauses, position updates stop, UI becomes unresponsive
- The BLE connection does not cleanly disconnect â€” it hangs in limbo waiting for the radio to reappear
- Recovery: force close GroupTrack, move radio back within range, reopen app
- Prevention: leave the radio mounted in your cart. Keep your phone in the cart. They travel together.

### Pre-Ride Checklist

- [ ] Phone charged
- [ ] Radio charged and firmware at 2.6.11 or earlier
- [ ] Radio mounted in cart (stays with phone during ride)
- [ ] GroupTrack installed and opens without errors
- [ ] Radio connects via Bluetooth (solid connection icon)
- [ ] Map tiles downloaded for ride area (check blue overlay on Planning Map)
- [ ] Trail data downloaded for ride area
- [ ] GPS lock acquired (position shows on map)

---

## INSTALLATION

### Installing GroupTrack APK

**From Play Store (tester):**
- Accept tester invitation link
- Download from Play Store
- Package: com.grouptrack.android

**From local APK (developer/tester):**
```bash
# Android 1 â€” V2.4 tester device
adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 install -r -d app/build/outputs/apk/google/debug/app-google-universal-debug.apk

# Android 2 â€” V3.0 dev device
adb -s 24039703201775 install -r -d app/build/outputs/apk/google/debug/app-google-universal-debug.apk
```

**âš ï¸ INSTALL RULE: Always use `-r -d` flags.**
Never omit `-r -d` â€” doing so wipes tile cache, app data, and config.

**âš ï¸ Play Store vs Local APK: Different signing keys.**
Must uninstall one before installing the other. Cannot have both.

### Post-Install Steps

1. Launch GroupTrack
2. Grant location permission when prompted
3. If duplicate launcher icon appears: `adb shell pm clear com.android.launcher3`
4. Open Planning Map and verify tile loading
5. Connect radio â€” should auto-discover via Bluetooth

### Radio Setup

1. Power on T1000-E radio
2. **Verify firmware is 2.6.11 or earlier** â€” DO NOT UPDATE
3. Open GroupTrack â†’ radio should appear in device list
4. Select radio to pair
5. Verify connection: position icon, signal strength visible

### Device Compatibility

| Device | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Android 1 (8624SBCEDF00001789) | âœ… Validated | V2.4 tester device |
| Android 2 (24039703201775) | âœ… Validated | V3.0 dev device (no GPS) |
| P10_T (P10V07162601000362) | âœ… Validated | 3GB RAM, Android 16 |
| Tab8NEU / budget tablets | âŒ Not compatible | Cannot hold BLE to T1000-E. Supervision timeout 0x0008 after 8-10 seconds. Hardware issue, not app bug. |

---

## TROUBLESHOOTING

### BLE Connection Issues

**Symptom: App freezes or pauses during ride**
- **Cause:** Radio moved beyond Bluetooth range (~50') while still connected. BLE supervision timeout.
- **Fix:** Force close GroupTrack. Move radio back within range of phone. Reopen app.
- **Prevention:** Keep radio mounted in cart with phone. They must stay within 50' of each other at all times during a ride.

**Symptom: Radio connects then disconnects repeatedly (8-10 second cycle)**
- **Cause:** Device hardware incompatibility (Tab8NEU, budget Android tablets). Supervision timeout reason 0x0008.
- **Fix:** Use a compatible device (see Device Compatibility table above). This is a hardware issue, not an app bug.

**Symptom: Radio won't connect at all after firmware update**
- **Cause:** T1000-E firmware updated beyond 2.6.11.
- **Fix:** Flash radio back to firmware 2.6.11 using Meshtastic Flasher tool. Do NOT use any firmware newer than 2.6.11.

**Symptom: Radio connects but position doesn't update**
- **Cause:** Radio may be out of GPS fix, or BLE connection is degraded.
- **Fix:** Check radio has clear sky view for GPS. Force close and reconnect. Verify radio firmware is 2.6.11.

### Map and Tile Issues

**Symptom: Map shows blank/grey tiles**
- **Cause:** No tile cache for this area. Online tiles failed to load (no connectivity or tile source down).
- **Fix:** Check connectivity. Download tiles for this area while on WiFi. Check blue overlay on Planning Map to confirm tile coverage.

**Symptom: Double labels on satellite map**
- **Cause:** Old cached tiles (downloaded with hybrid URL) showing baked-in labels plus new overlay labels.
- **Fix:** Clear tile cache for affected area and re-download with current tile source URL.

**Symptom: Map tiles load online but show blank offline**
- **Cause:** Tiles not downloaded for this area.
- **Fix:** Before going to the field, download tiles for your ride area using Planning Map download function. Verify blue overlay covers your ride area.

### Trail Display Issues

**Symptom: No trails showing on map**
- **Cause:** No trail source downloaded, or trail database not loaded.
- **Fix:** Open Planning Map â†’ Trail Sources â†’ select and download a source (e.g., UGRC Utah Trails).

**Symptom: Trails showing in wrong location**
- **Cause:** Coordinate system mismatch or corrupt GeoJSON source.
- **Fix:** Remove trail source and re-download/re-ingest.

### App Issues

**Symptom: ANR (App Not Responding) on launch**
- **Cause:** Blocking operation on main thread.
- **Fix:** Force close and reopen. If persistent, report with logcat output.

**Symptom: Duplicate launcher icons**
- **Fix:** Run `adb shell pm clear com.android.launcher3` to clear launcher cache.

**Symptom: App data lost after update**
- **Cause:** Installed without `-r -d` flags, or switched between Play Store and local APK.
- **Fix:** Always install with `adb install -r -d`. Uninstall opposite signing key version before installing.
- **Recovery:** User spatial data in /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/data/ survives uninstall. Tile cache in /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/maps/tiles/ survives uninstall. Only app-internal data is lost.

### Radio Firmware Reference

| Firmware | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| 2.6.11 | âœ… APPROVED | Maximum recommended version for T1000-E |
| 2.6.12+ | âŒ DO NOT USE | Destabilizes BLE and radio configuration |
| < 2.6.11 | âœ… OK | Earlier versions work but may lack features |

### Emergency Recovery

If everything is broken:
1. Uninstall GroupTrack
2. Flash T1000-E radio to firmware 2.6.11
3. Reinstall GroupTrack APK with `adb install -r -d`
4. Launch app â€” spatial data in Documents/GroupTrack/ should still be there
5. Reconnect radio
6. Re-download tiles if cache was lost

# GroupTrack Tick Engine Reference
## ConvoyViewModel.kt tick() + ConvoyEngine.kt

---

## TICK CYCLE OVERVIEW (every TICK_MS milliseconds)

```
tick()
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 1. GET NODES
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Simulation mode: ConvoySimulation.tick(nowMs)
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Live mode: readLiveNodes(nowMs)
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 2. SELF-HEAL LEAD ASSIGNMENT
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ If recording + 1 node + no lead â†’ auto-assign that node as lead
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 3. CONVOY ENGINE COMPUTE â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ computeStatus(node, nowMs)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ age = nowMs - node.lastSeenMs
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ age >= LOST_MINUTES    â†’ LOST (removed from active)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ age >= SIGNAL_DROP_MIN â†’ SIGNAL_DROP (still in active)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ else                   â†’ ACTIVE
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ computeHeading(nodes)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Median heading of ACTIVE nodes moving > 3mph
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Returns convoy direction of travel
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ computeSortPositions(nodes, heading)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Projects each node's lat/lon onto the heading vector
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Sorts DESCENDING by projection (front â†’ back)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Assigns convoyPosition: 1 = front, N = back
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ LOST nodes appended at end
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ assignLeadTail(sorted, lockedLeadNodeId, tailNodeId)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Lead: LOCKED by nodeId (set via dialog, never changes)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Lead is NULL if locked node is not in active list
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Tail: by tailNodeId or fallback to max convoyPosition
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ computeSpan(lead, tail)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Haversine miles between lead and tail
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ computeProximity(nodes, myCartId)
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ For each node: feetToNodeAhead, feetToNodeBehind
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ milesToLead, milesToTail
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ Sets isMyCart flag
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 4. FEED RADIO GPS (if device has no GPS hardware)
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ useRadioGps == true â†’ feed myCart position to GPS service
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Only for devices WITHOUT GPS hardware
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 5. DEBUG LOGGING
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Logs: lead callsign, trackFrom nodeId, locked flag, distance accum
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 6. TRAIL ACCUMULATION â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ LEAD-ONLY MODE (_trackLeadOnly == true)
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Gets leadNode from state.lead
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ *** IF LEAD IS NULL â†’ ENTIRE BLOCK SKIPPED ***
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Compares to lastLeadLat/lastLeadLon
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ If position changed â†’ create LeadTrackSegment
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Adds segment to _routeTrailSegments
  â”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Updates lastLeadLat/lastLeadLon
  â”‚     â”‚
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ MULTI-CART MODE (_trackLeadOnly == false)
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ Iterates ALL state.nodes
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ Skips nodes with lat=0, lon=0
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ Compares to lastNodePositions[nodeId]
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ If position changed â†’ create segment
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ *** 0.25mi JUMP FILTER *** (still present on multi path)
  â”‚           â””â”€â”€ Updates lastNodePositions[nodeId]
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 7. OFF-TRACK DETECTION
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ For each node, compute min distance to any trail segment
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ If > OFF_TRACK_MILES threshold â†’ mark as off-track
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€ 8. COLOR SEGMENTS
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Lead-only: all segments black
  â”‚     â””â”€â”€ Multi-track: each node's segments get node's markerColor
  â”‚
  â””â”€â”€ 9. UPDATE SELECTED NODE HUD
        â””â”€â”€ Refresh selected node data if HUD is showing node detail
```

---

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES

| Variable | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `lastLeadLat/Lon` | Double? | Lead cart's last position THIS SESSION |
| `lastNodePositions` | Map<String, Pair<Double,Double>> | All carts' last positions THIS SESSION |
| `currentLeadNodeId` | String? | Currently tracked lead node ID |
| `lockedLeadNodeId` | String? | Permanently locked lead (never changes) |
| `_routeTrailSegments` | List<LeadTrackSegment> | Accumulated trail segments |
| `_leadTrackSegments` | List<LeadTrackSegment> | Colored segments for display |
| `nodeDistanceAccum` | Map<String, Double> | Per-node distance traveled |

---

## CONVOY ORDER DETERMINATION

Convoy order is computed EVERY TICK by `computeSortPositions`:

1. Calculate convoy heading from median of active moving nodes
2. Project each node position onto the heading vector: `lat * cos(heading) + lon * sin(heading)`
3. Sort descending â€” highest projection = furthest along route = position 1 (LEAD)
4. LOST nodes are appended at end (not sorted)

**This means convoy order is DYNAMIC** â€” it changes as carts move and pass each other.

---

## THE LEAD DROPOUT PROBLEM (Task 2)

### Current behavior:
```
state.lead is populated by assignLeadTail()
  â””â”€â”€ Finds node matching lockedLeadNodeId
  â””â”€â”€ If that node is LOST â†’ not in active list â†’ state.lead = NULL
  â””â”€â”€ tick() line 577: if (leadNode != null) { ... }
  â””â”€â”€ leadNode is null â†’ trail block SKIPPED â†’ track display freezes
```

### Required behavior:
```
For EVERY cart on EVERY tick:
  1. Cart is ACTIVE with valid position â†’ use its reported position
  2. Cart is SIGNAL_DROP or LOST â†’ use lastKnownPosition
  3. Check cart behind (next convoyPosition) â†’ if behind cart is
     FURTHER ALONG than this cart's lastKnownPosition â†’ substitute
     behind cart's position as this cart's new lastKnownPosition
  4. Draw segment from previous position to new position â€” ALWAYS
  5. Track line NEVER goes backwards
```

### "Further along" test:
Use the same heading projection as computeSortPositions:
```
projection = lat * cos(heading) + lon * sin(heading)
```
If trailing cart's projection > this cart's lastKnown projection â†’ trailing cart is ahead â†’ substitute.

|---|---|---|

=== GroupTrack_V25_DataProtection_v1.md ===
# GroupTrack V2.5 â€” Data Protection: Backup, Journal, Rollback
## Schema Hardening Prerequisite
## May 9, 2026

---

## 1. THE PROBLEM

The user spatial database (grouptrack_user.spatialite) contains irreplaceable personal data: waypoints, routes, tracks, ride areas. A bad import, an accidental bulk delete, a corrupt consolidation, or a failed source ingestion could destroy rider data that took months to build. 

Three layers of protection required:
- **Backup** â€” full database snapshots, recoverable
- **Journal** â€” every change logged with before-state, reversible
- **Rollback** â€” undo to a specific point in time

---

## 2. BACKUP

### Automatic backup:
- On app launch: copy grouptrack_user.spatialite to grouptrack_user.backup
- Before any destructive operation (source removal, area removal, bulk delete): create timestamped backup
- Location: /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/data/backups/
- Naming: grouptrack_user_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.backup
- Retain last 5 backups. Delete oldest when creating 6th.
- Never auto-delete backups during storage cleanup â€” only the backup rotation.

### Manual backup:
- Settings â†’ Data Management â†’ Backup Now
- Creates timestamped backup immediately
- User can also export to Downloads for off-device storage

### Recovery:
- Settings â†’ Data Management â†’ Restore from Backup
- Shows list of available backups with timestamp and size
- User selects backup â†’ confirmation: "This will replace all current waypoints, routes, tracks, and ride areas with the backup from [date]. This cannot be undone."
- Restore = close current DB, copy backup over current, reopen
- After restore, create a backup of what was just replaced (so user can undo the restore)

### Backup schema:
```sql
CREATE TABLE backup_log (
    backup_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    filename        TEXT NOT NULL,           -- backup file name
    created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- ISO 8601
    trigger_reason  TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'app_launch' | 'pre_destructive' | 'manual' | 'pre_restore'
    description     TEXT,                    -- what operation triggered this backup
    size_bytes      INTEGER NOT NULL,        -- backup file size
    waypoint_count  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,       -- snapshot counts for display
    route_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    track_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    area_count      INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);
```

---

## 3. CHANGE JOURNAL

Every INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE on user data tables is journaled with enough detail to reverse the operation.

### Journal table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE change_journal (
    journal_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    transaction_id  TEXT NOT NULL,           -- UUID grouping related changes
    sequence        INTEGER NOT NULL,        -- order within transaction (1, 2, 3...)
    timestamp       TEXT NOT NULL,           -- ISO 8601
    table_name      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'waypoints' | 'routes' | 'tracks' | 'ride_areas'
    operation       TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'INSERT' | 'UPDATE' | 'DELETE'
    record_id       TEXT NOT NULL,           -- primary key of affected record
    before_state    TEXT,                    -- JSON snapshot of record BEFORE change (NULL for INSERT)
    after_state     TEXT,                    -- JSON snapshot of record AFTER change (NULL for DELETE)
    user_action     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- human-readable: 'Created waypoint "Gas Station"'
    rolled_back     INTEGER DEFAULT 0       -- 1 if this change was rolled back
);

CREATE INDEX idx_journal_transaction ON change_journal(transaction_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_journal_timestamp ON change_journal(timestamp);
CREATE INDEX idx_journal_table ON change_journal(table_name, record_id);
```

### What gets journaled:

| Table | INSERT | UPDATE | DELETE |
|-------|--------|--------|--------|
| waypoints | Full record as after_state | Before + after state | Full record as before_state |
| routes | Full record as after_state | Before + after state | Full record as before_state |
| tracks | Full record as after_state | Before + after state | Full record as before_state |
| ride_areas | Full record as after_state | Before + after state | Full record as before_state |
| tile_sources | Full record as after_state | Before + after state | Full record as before_state |
| map_slots | N/A | Before + after state | N/A |

### What does NOT get journaled:
- Trail data (grouptrack_trails.db) â€” public data, re-downloadable, no user data at risk
- Transfer queue â€” transient operational data
- Transfer history â€” audit data, not user content
- data_log â€” already a log, don't log the log
- backup_log â€” metadata, not user content

### Transaction grouping:
Related changes share a transaction_id. Examples:
- Waypoint consolidation: DELETE waypoint A + UPDATE waypoint B = one transaction, two journal entries
- Source ingestion: all trail INSERTs share one transaction (but trails aren't journaled â€” only user data tables)
- Bulk waypoint import from ride enrollment (V3.0): all INSERTs share one transaction

### Journal triggers (one per table per operation):

```sql
-- WAYPOINT INSERT
CREATE TRIGGER jrnl_waypoint_insert AFTER INSERT ON waypoints
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO change_journal (
        transaction_id, sequence, timestamp, table_name, operation,
        record_id, before_state, after_state, user_action
    ) VALUES (
        COALESCE(@current_transaction_id, hex(randomblob(16))),
        COALESCE(@current_sequence, 1),
        datetime('now'),
        'waypoints', 'INSERT',
        NEW.waypoint_id,
        NULL,
        json_object(
            'waypoint_id', NEW.waypoint_id,
            'name', NEW.name,
            'type', NEW.type,
            'description', NEW.description,
            'area_id', NEW.area_id,
            'ride_id', NEW.ride_id,
            'shared', NEW.shared,
            'created_at', NEW.created_at,
            'updated_at', NEW.updated_at
        ),
        'Created waypoint "' || NEW.name || '"'
    );
END;

-- WAYPOINT UPDATE
CREATE TRIGGER jrnl_waypoint_update AFTER UPDATE ON waypoints
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO change_journal (
        transaction_id, sequence, timestamp, table_name, operation,
        record_id, before_state, after_state, user_action
    ) VALUES (
        COALESCE(@current_transaction_id, hex(randomblob(16))),
        COALESCE(@current_sequence, 1),
        datetime('now'),
        'waypoints', 'UPDATE',
        NEW.waypoint_id,
        json_object(
            'waypoint_id', OLD.waypoint_id,
            'name', OLD.name,
            'type', OLD.type,
            'description', OLD.description,
            'area_id', OLD.area_id,
            'ride_id', OLD.ride_id,
            'shared', OLD.shared,
            'created_at', OLD.created_at,
            'updated_at', OLD.updated_at
        ),
        json_object(
            'waypoint_id', NEW.waypoint_id,
            'name', NEW.name,
            'type', NEW.type,
            'description', NEW.description,
            'area_id', NEW.area_id,
            'ride_id', NEW.ride_id,
            'shared', NEW.shared,
            'created_at', NEW.created_at,
            'updated_at', NEW.updated_at
        ),
        CASE
            WHEN OLD.name != NEW.name THEN 'Renamed waypoint "' || OLD.name || '" to "' || NEW.name || '"'
            WHEN OLD.type != NEW.type THEN 'Changed type of "' || NEW.name || '"'
            WHEN OLD.shared != NEW.shared THEN CASE NEW.shared WHEN 1 THEN 'Shared waypoint "' || NEW.name || '"' ELSE 'Unshared waypoint "' || NEW.name || '"' END
            ELSE 'Updated waypoint "' || NEW.name || '"'
        END
    );
END;

-- WAYPOINT DELETE
CREATE TRIGGER jrnl_waypoint_delete BEFORE DELETE ON waypoints
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO change_journal (
        transaction_id, sequence, timestamp, table_name, operation,
        record_id, before_state, after_state, user_action
    ) VALUES (
        COALESCE(@current_transaction_id, hex(randomblob(16))),
        COALESCE(@current_sequence, 1),
        datetime('now'),
        'waypoints', 'DELETE',
        OLD.waypoint_id,
        json_object(
            'waypoint_id', OLD.waypoint_id,
            'name', OLD.name,
            'type', OLD.type,
            'description', OLD.description,
            'area_id', OLD.area_id,
            'ride_id', OLD.ride_id,
            'shared', OLD.shared,
            'created_at', OLD.created_at,
            'updated_at', OLD.updated_at
        ),
        NULL,
        'Deleted waypoint "' || OLD.name || '"'
    );
END;
```

Same pattern for routes, tracks, ride_areas â€” three triggers each (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). 12 journal triggers total across 4 tables.

---

## 4. ROLLBACK

### Single operation undo:
- "Undo last action" available immediately after any change
- Reads the most recent journal entry (or transaction group)
- Reverses the operation:
  - INSERT â†’ DELETE the record
  - DELETE â†’ INSERT from before_state JSON
  - UPDATE â†’ UPDATE with before_state values
- Mark journal entry as rolled_back=1
- Log the rollback as a new journal entry

### Transaction rollback:
- All entries sharing a transaction_id are rolled back together
- Rolled back in reverse sequence order (last change first)
- Example: waypoint consolidation rollback = re-INSERT deleted waypoint A, then revert UPDATE on waypoint B

### Point-in-time rollback:
- Settings â†’ Data Management â†’ Rollback to Date/Time
- Show list of transactions with timestamps and descriptions
- User selects a point â†’ ALL transactions after that point are rolled back in reverse order
- Confirmation: "Roll back N changes made since [date/time]? This will undo: [list of user_action descriptions]"
- After rollback, create a backup of the pre-rollback state (so rollback itself can be undone)

### Rollback limitations:
- Cannot rollback geometry changes on waypoints (SpatiaLite geometry not stored in JSON before_state). SOLUTION: store geometry as WKT text in the before_state JSON.
- Cannot rollback file operations (track file deleted from filesystem). SOLUTION: journal stores the fact, but actual file recovery requires the backup. Rollback of track DELETE recreates the DB record but warns: "Track file may need to be restored from backup."
- Cannot rollback trail source ingestion (trails are in separate DB, not journaled). SOLUTION: trail re-ingestion is the recovery path â€” re-download and re-ingest the source.

### Rollback UI:
```
â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚ CHANGE HISTORY                           â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ Today                                    â”‚
â”‚ 3:42 PM  Deleted waypoint "Old Gate"     â”‚
â”‚          [UNDO]                          â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ 3:38 PM  Consolidated "Gas Station"      â”‚
â”‚          into "Chevron Fuel Stop"        â”‚
â”‚          [UNDO]                          â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ 3:15 PM  Created waypoint "Trailhead"   â”‚
â”‚          [UNDO]                          â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ 2:50 PM  Renamed route "Bar 10 Day 1"   â”‚
â”‚          [UNDO]                          â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ Yesterday                                â”‚
â”‚ ...                                      â”‚
â”‚                                          â”‚
â”‚ [ROLLBACK TO DATE...]                    â”‚
â”‚ [RESTORE FROM BACKUP...]                 â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
```

---

## 5. JOURNAL MAINTENANCE

### Size management:
- Journal grows with every change. Needs periodic cleanup.
- Retain last 30 days of journal entries by default.
- Entries older than 30 days: purge (DELETE WHERE timestamp < date('now', '-30 days') AND rolled_back = 0)
- Rolled-back entries purge after 7 days.
- Before purge: create a backup (so data is recoverable even after journal cleanup).

### Journal + backup interaction:
- Backup captures the full database state at a point in time
- Journal captures individual changes between backups
- Recovery strategy: restore backup + replay journal forward to desired point
- Simpler recovery: just restore the backup closest to desired state

---

## 6. GEOMETRY IN JOURNAL

Waypoint geometry (POINT) and route geometry (LINESTRING) must be captured in the journal for complete rollback.

### Solution â€” store as WKT in JSON:
```sql
-- In trigger, capture geometry as WKT text
json_object(
    'waypoint_id', OLD.waypoint_id,
    'name', OLD.name,
    'geometry_wkt', AsText(OLD.geometry),  -- 'POINT(-113.5 37.1)'
    ...
)

-- On rollback, recreate geometry from WKT
UPDATE waypoints SET geometry = GeomFromText(
    json_extract(before_state, '$.geometry_wkt'), 4326
) WHERE waypoint_id = ?;
```

This captures the exact position in the journal so moved or deleted waypoints can be perfectly restored.

---

## 7. IMPACT ON SCHEMA

### New tables to add to grouptrack_user.spatialite:
- change_journal (12 triggers: 3 per table Ã— 4 tables)
- backup_log (metadata for backup management)

### Schema version:
- Add schema_version to db_metadata: version 2 includes journal and backup tables
- On app launch: if schema_version < 2, run migration to add new tables and triggers
- Migration is non-destructive â€” adds tables, doesn't modify existing data

---

## 8. STANDING RULES

1. Every user data change is journaled. No exceptions.
2. Backup before every destructive operation. Automatic, not optional.
3. Journal stores before AND after state. Both needed for rollback.
4. Geometry stored as WKT in journal for spatial rollback.
5. Journal retained 30 days. Backups retained last 5.
6. Rollback of a rollback is possible (backup created before rollback executes).
7. Trail data (public, re-downloadable) is NOT journaled â€” recovery is re-ingestion.
8. Track file recovery requires backup â€” journal only tracks DB record, not filesystem.

---

*GroupTrack V2.5 | Data Protection Specification v1 | May 9, 2026*
*Schema must include journal and backup tables before any application code.*


=== GroupTrack_V25_EntityLifecycle_v1.md ===
# GroupTrack V2.5 â€” Entity Lifecycle Scenarios
## Maintenance Operations and Spatial Model Impact
## May 9, 2026 â€” Schema hardening prerequisite

---

## Purpose

Every operation on every spatial entity must be defined BEFORE triggers are written. Each scenario answers: what can the user do, what changes in the database, what cascades to other tables, what gets logged, and what business rules can block the operation.

This document defines trigger requirements. No application code until these scenarios are reviewed and confirmed.

---

## 1. TRACKS

Source of truth: GPX/KML file in Documents/my_tracks/
Database role: spatial index (metadata + bounding box) in grouptrack_user.spatialite

### 1.1 Track Created (GPS Recording)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | GPS recording stops, file saved to my_tracks/ |
| Primary action | INSERT into tracks table: filename, name, bbox, recorded_at, distance, duration, max_speed, elevation_gain, source_format |
| Spatial impact | Calculate bbox from GPS points. Check which ride_areas this bbox intersects. Update has_spatial=1 on intersecting areas. |
| Log | data_log: action='track_created', track_count=1 |
| Shared flag | Default shared=0. If ride is active AND ride.private=false, prompt "Share this track?" If yes, shared=1. If ride.private=true, suppress prompt, shared=0. |
| Ride link | If recorded during an active ride, set ride_id on track record |
| Business rules | None â€” tracks can always be created |

### 1.2 Track Imported (from Downloads)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User imports GPX/KML via Import screen or file picker |
| Primary action | File copied to my_tracks/. INSERT into tracks table with metadata. |
| Spatial impact | Same as 1.1 â€” calculate bbox, update intersecting ride_areas |
| Log | data_log: action='track_imported', track_count=1 (or N if multi-track split) |
| Date rule | Set file mtime from earliest <time> element (existing ConvoyTrackOps behavior) |
| Duplicate check | If filename already exists in my_tracks/, skip with status. No overwrite. |
| Business rules | Source file stays in Downloads as backup. Never auto-delete source. |

### 1.3 Track Renamed

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User renames track via action sheet |
| Primary action | File renamed in my_tracks/. UPDATE tracks SET filename=new, name=new WHERE track_id=? |
| Spatial impact | None â€” bbox unchanged, area coverage unchanged |
| Log | data_log: action='track_renamed', source=track_id |
| Cross-entity | If this track was converted to a route (routes.source_track_id = this track_id), does the route name update? DECISION NEEDED: No â€” route name is independent once created. The link is for provenance only. |
| Business rules | Cannot rename to a name that already exists (existing RenameResult.NameExists behavior) |

### 1.4 Track Deleted

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User deletes track via action sheet with confirmation dialog |
| Primary action | File deleted from my_tracks/. DELETE FROM tracks WHERE track_id=? |
| Spatial impact | Recalculate has_spatial for affected ride_areas. If no tracks, waypoints, or routes remain in area, set has_spatial=0. |
| Log | data_log: action='track_deleted', track_count=1 |
| Cross-entity | If track was shared (shared=1), the shared copy in V3.0 collective is NOT affected â€” local delete doesn't remove from server. If track was converted to a route, the route remains â€” source_track_id becomes a dead reference (acceptable â€” route stands on its own). |
| Business rules | ALWAYS requires confirmation dialog with filename and size. Never auto-delete. Cannot delete if file is currently being recorded (active GPS recording). |

### 1.5 Track Shared

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps "Share" on track action sheet, or responds "Yes" to post-recording prompt |
| Primary action | UPDATE tracks SET shared=1 WHERE track_id=? |
| Spatial impact | None â€” shared flag doesn't affect local spatial model |
| Log | data_log: action='track_shared', source=track_id |
| Business rules | BLOCKED if track is linked to a ride AND ride.private=true. Show message: "This track was recorded on a private ride and cannot be shared." |
| V3.0 behavior | When upload engine activates, shared=1 tracks queue for upload. Until then, flag only. |

### 1.6 Track Unshared

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps "Unshare" on track action sheet |
| Primary action | UPDATE tracks SET shared=0 WHERE track_id=? |
| Spatial impact | None |
| Log | data_log: action='track_unshared', source=track_id |
| V3.0 impact | If already uploaded to collective, local unshare does NOT remove from server. Server removal is a separate action in V3.0. |
| Business rules | Always allowed |

### 1.7 Track Converted to Route

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps "Convert to Route" on track action sheet |
| Primary action | INSERT into routes: geometry copied from track GPX/KML, source_track_id=track_id, name=track_name + " (route)" |
| Spatial impact | New route has geometry â†’ update ride_areas has_spatial for intersecting areas |
| Log | data_log: action='track_to_route', source=track_id |
| Cross-entity | Track remains unchanged. Route is a new independent entity linked by source_track_id. |
| Business rules | Always allowed. Does not modify or delete the original track. |

### 1.8 Track Smoothed (snap to trail)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps "Smooth Track" on track action sheet |
| Primary action | Read GPS points from file. For each point, snap to nearest trail in grouptrack_trails.db. Write smoothed geometry. User choice: save as new file (original preserved) or overwrite with confirmation. |
| Spatial impact | Bbox may change slightly. UPDATE tracks SET bbox=new_bbox. Recalculate area intersections. |
| Log | data_log: action='track_smoothed', source=track_id |
| Business rules | Original file preserved by default. Overwrite requires explicit confirmation. |

### 1.9 Track File Sync (orphan detection)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | App launch scan of my_tracks/ directory |
| Scenario A | File exists, no DB record â†’ INSERT record (same as 1.2 but auto-detected) |
| Scenario B | DB record exists, no file â†’ DELETE record (orphan cleanup). Update area coverage. Log. |
| Scenario C | File renamed outside app â†’ old DB record orphaned (Scenario B), new file detected (Scenario A). Net effect: record recreated with new filename. |
| Business rules | Scan is read-only on files. Never delete files during scan. Only reconcile DB records. |

### 1.10 Track Impact Summary â€” All Operations

| Operation | Spatial DB Impact | Area Coverage | Log Entry | Cross-Entity |
|-----------|------------------|---------------|-----------|--------------|
| ADD (record) | Insert record with bbox | has_spatial=1 on intersecting areas | track_created | None |
| ADD (import) | Copy file + insert record | has_spatial=1 on intersecting areas | track_imported | Source file preserved |
| RENAME | Update filename + name fields | None | track_renamed | Converted route name NOT updated |
| DELETE | Remove file + delete record | Recalculate has_spatial â€” may flip to 0 | track_deleted | Converted route remains (dead source_track_id). Shared copy unaffected. |
| SHARE | Set shared=1 | None | track_shared | BLOCKED if ride.private=true |
| UNSHARE | Set shared=0 | None | track_unshared | Server copy unaffected |
| CONVERT TO ROUTE | Insert new route record | Route adds to area coverage | track_to_route | Track unchanged. Route is independent. |
| SMOOTH | Update geometry in file, update bbox | Bbox may change â€” recalculate areas | track_smoothed | None |
| FILE SYNC | Reconcile DB with filesystem | Add/remove records as needed | track_synced | Orphan records cleaned |

---

## 2. TRAILS

Source of truth: grouptrack_trails.db (SQLite)
Population: ingested from agency GeoJSON sources
Access: read-only after ingestion

### 2.1 Trail Source Ingested (first time)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User selects source from catalog, applies filters, downloads and ingests |
| Primary action | Parse GeoJSON features. Apply user filters. For each matching feature: normalize properties via schema_map, calculate bbox and length, INSERT into trails table. |
| Spatial impact | Trails added. Viewport queries return new trails on next pan/zoom. |
| Source tracking | INSERT into source_ingestions: source_id, version_ingested, trail_count, filters_used |
| Dedup | For each trail, run dedup check against existing trails. CONFIRMED dupes auto-skip. PROBABLE/POSSIBLE dupes queued for review screen. |
| Log | data_log: action='source_ingested', source=source_id, trail_count=N |
| Business rules | User must confirm download before ingestion starts. Show estimated size and feature count from catalog. |

### 2.2 Trail Source Re-ingested (refresh/update)

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps refresh on a source with available update (version check shows newer) |
| Primary action | DELETE all trails WHERE source_id matches this source. Re-ingest from fresh download with same filters (preserved in source_ingestions.filters_used). |
| Spatial impact | Trails replaced. Some trail_ids change (new UUIDs generated). |
| Source tracking | UPDATE source_ingestions: version_ingested=new, ingested_at=now, trail_count=new |
| Cross-entity | User waypoints snapped to old trail positions remain valid â€” waypoints have independent coordinates, not references to trail geometry. |
| Log | data_log: action='source_refreshed', source=source_id, trail_count=N |
| Business rules | Warn user: "This will replace X trails from [source]. Your waypoints and tracks are not affected." Require confirmation. |

### 2.3 Trail Source Removed

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User removes a trail source entirely |
| Primary action | DELETE FROM trails WHERE source_agency matches AND source ingestion record matches. DELETE FROM source_ingestions WHERE source_id=?. |
| Spatial impact | Trails removed from viewport queries. Map shows fewer trails. |
| Cross-entity | User waypoints remain â€” they have independent coordinates. User tracks remain â€” they reference files, not trails. Routes remain â€” they have independent geometry. |
| Log | data_log: action='source_removed', source=source_id, trail_count=N_deleted |
| Business rules | Confirmation: "Remove X trails from [source]? Your waypoints, tracks, and routes are not affected." |

### 2.4 Trail Hidden by User

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | User taps a trail and selects "Hide" (future feature) |
| Primary action | UPDATE trails SET is_hidden=1 WHERE trail_id=? (requires new column) |
| Spatial impact | Hidden trails excluded from viewport queries (WHERE is_hidden=0) |
| Business rules | Can unhide. Hidden state is local â€” re-ingestion resets hidden state. |
| DECISION NEEDED | Is this a V2.5 feature or deferred? Recommend deferred â€” low priority. |

### 2.5 Duplicate Detected During Ingestion

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Trigger | Dedup check during ingestion finds spatial overlap |
| CONFIRMED dupe | Auto-skip incoming trail. INSERT into dedup_log: resolution='auto_skip'. Increment source_ingestions.dupes_skipped. |
| PROBABLE dupe | Add to review queue. Present on review screen with mini-map comparison. User resolves: KEEP EXISTING, REPLACE, KEEP BOTH. |
| POSSIBLE dupe | Same as PROBABLE but with stronger warning that these may be different trails. |
| KEEP EXISTING | Skip incoming. Log resolution='user_keep_existing'. |
| REPLACE | DELETE existing trail. INSERT incoming. Log resolution='user_replace'. |
| KEEP BOTH | INSERT incoming alongside existing. Log resolution='user_keep_both'. |
| Business rules | First source ingested wins auto-resolve. User can always override. |

### 2.6 Trail Impact Summary â€” All Operations

| Operation | Spatial DB Impact | Area Coverage | Log Entry | Cross-Entity |
|-----------|------------------|---------------|-----------|--------------|
| SOURCE INGESTED | Batch insert trails | Viewport queries return new trails | source_ingested | Dedup against existing sources |
| SOURCE REFRESHED | Delete old + re-insert all | Trail_ids change (new UUIDs) | source_refreshed | User waypoints/tracks/routes UNAFFECTED |
| SOURCE REMOVED | Delete all trails from source | Fewer trails in viewport | source_removed | User data UNAFFECTED. Snap-to may have gaps. |
| DUPE AUTO-SKIP | No insert | None | dedup auto_skip | Dedup log entry |
| DUPE USER REPLACE | Delete existing + insert new | Trail replaced in viewport | dedup user_replace | Dedup log entry |
